headline: SSC 2026 results published: Overall pass rate drops to 62.25%, GPA-5 recipients decrease
summary: The average pass rate across all 11 education boards fell by 3.99% compared to last year, with a significant reduction in students achieving a GPA-5.
details: The results for the SSC and equivalent examinations for 2026 have been published. The results were released simultaneously across all education boards in the country on Monday, August 10, at 10 AM.
This year, the average pass rate across all 11 education boards (9 general, Madrasa, and Technical boards) stood at 62.25%. A total of 116,676 candidates achieved a GPA-5.
For the 9 general education boards, the average pass rate was 64.05%, a decrease from last year's 68.04%. This marks a 3.99% drop in the pass rate compared to the previous year.
The number of students achieving GPA-5 in SSC also saw a reduction, with 106,009 candidates receiving it this year, down from 125,018 last year.

The results were made available simultaneously from respective educational institutions and online. Education Minister A. N. M. Ehsanul Hoque Milon inaugurated the result publication program at an event held at the Ministry of Education.
caption:
Bangladesh's SSC and equivalent exam results for 2026 are out, revealing a notable drop in the overall pass rate and the number of students achieving a GPA-5.

The results for the SSC and equivalent examinations for 2026 have been published. The results were released simultaneously across all education boards in the country on Monday, August 10, at 10 AM.

This year, the average pass rate across all 11 education boards (9 general, Madrasa, and Technical boards) stood at 62.25%. A total of 116,676 candidates achieved a GPA-5.

For the 9 general education boards, the average pass rate was 64.05%, a decrease from last year's 68.04%. This marks a 3.99% drop in the pass rate compared to the previous year.

The number of students achieving GPA-5 in SSC also saw a reduction, with 106,009 candidates receiving it this year, down from 125,018 last year.

The results were made available simultaneously from respective educational institutions and online. Education Minister A. N. M. Ehsanul Hoque Milon inaugurated the result publication program at an event held at the Ministry of Education.

headline_marked: [[16 Bangladeshis killed]] in devastating Saudi sofa factory fire in Riyadh
headline: 16 Bangladeshis killed in devastating Saudi sofa factory fire in Riyadh
summary: A massive blaze erupted at a sofa factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, claiming the lives of 16 Bangladeshi expatriate workers. Authorities are working to identify the victims and provide support.
details: At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire that broke out at a sofa factory in the Musa Industrial Area under the Al-Shifa police station in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The incident occurred around 2:00 PM yesterday, with all 16 victims reportedly dying on the spot.

According to the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, 13 of the deceased hailed from Naogaon, two from Natore, and one from Rajshahi. Witnesses at the scene confirmed that all the victims were from Bangladesh.

The local fire service was still conducting rescue operations when the Ministry issued its notification. The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh has expressed deep sorrow over the incident and has officials on site, maintaining close contact with Saudi authorities to identify the victims.
caption:
A devastating fire at a sofa factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has claimed the lives of 16 Bangladeshi expatriate workers.

At least 16 Bangladeshi nationals were killed in a devastating fire that broke out at a sofa factory in the Musa Industrial Area under the Al-Shifa police station in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The incident occurred around 2:00 PM yesterday, with all 16 victims reportedly dying on the spot.

According to the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, 13 of the deceased hailed from Naogaon, two from Natore, and one from Rajshahi. Witnesses at the scene confirmed that all the victims were from Bangladesh.

The local fire service was still conducting rescue operations when the Ministry issued its notification. The Bangladesh Embassy in Riyadh has expressed deep sorrow over the incident and has officials on site, maintaining close contact with Saudi authorities to identify the victims.
